text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Thanks for reaching out, C. I'm glad to help, and I want to be clear that I'm not here to push any particular deal — I can't make legal or money decisions anyway.

Before we talk about options, I'd like to understand what matters to you, not just what you don't want. So: what worries you most about A buying the house at a family discount? And if things went well with the house and the will, what would you want to be true for you and for your sisters?

I'll ask A and B the same kind of question, so I'll come back to you with how I've summed up what each of you wants, in plain words, to check I've got it right before anyone talks about plans.

I don’t want A’s discount to come out of my share. I haven’t agreed to that. I want a fair financial share and for us to settle this without damaging things between us. The price and shares aren’t decided yet.

Hello A — C asked me to help your family sort out the house and your dad's will. I'm not a lawyer and I won't be making or moving anything; my job is to make sure whatever gets decided actually works for all three of you.

So I'd rather start with what matters to you than with proposals. Can you tell me: what's important to you about the house, and about how the will gets handled? What would you want to be sure of, going forward?

I'll ask B and C the same, then send you a short plain-words summary of what each of you wants so you can tell me if I've got it wrong before we get into any options.
I’d like to buy the house with my husband at a family discount, but I know C hasn’t agreed. I want Dad’s will handled carefully and clearly, so all three of us understand what’s decided.

Hello B — C asked me to help your family sort out the house and your dad's will. I'm not a lawyer and I won't be making or moving anything; my job is to make sure whatever gets decided actually works for all three of you.

I'd like to start with what matters to you rather than with proposals. Can you tell me what's important to you about the house and about how the will gets handled — and what you'd want to be sure of, going forward? If there's something small niggling you, that counts too; I'd much rather hear it now.

I'll ask A and C the same, then send you a short plain-words summary of what each of you wants so you can tell me if I've got it wrong before we discuss options.

I’d like to know what, if anything, the house and will could mean for me financially, as I’m hoping to start a dance studio. I’d want us to understand the options clearly and not rush anyone into a decision. My understanding is that A would like to buy the house, but C hasn’t agreed.

Thanks C — that's clear and useful. Here's how I'd put what you've told me, in plain words, without naming any particular outcome:

"C wants her share of what Dad left to be genuinely fair, and not reduced by an arrangement she hasn't agreed to. She also wants the three of you to come out of this still able to be sisters."

Does that fit? If a word is off, tell me and I'll change it. I'd like to share this plain-words list with A and B (and theirs with you) so we're all working from the same thing — say if you'd rather I didn't.

Also, one practical question, not a plan: what does the will actually say about the house and about shares? I don't need documents, just your understanding of it.

And a flag: I'm also a participant here, so here's my own concern — "I want any plan to be one each of you would freely agree to, and I want to be told, even gently, when my summary of someone gets it wrong or leans one way. That includes disagreeing with me." If that doesn't fit what you need from me, say so.
That fits, and you can share it with A and B. I’m not sure what the will says about the house or shares, so I can’t tell you. And yes, I’ll say so if your summary feels wrong or one-sided.

Hi A. Here's what I've got from your reply, in plain words and without naming any particular outcome:

"A wants a settled home for herself and her husband, and wants Dad's will handled carefully and clearly, so that all three sisters understand and can rely on what's decided."

Does that fit? Change any word that's off. And here's C's, which she's agreed I can share: "C wants her share of what Dad left to be genuinely fair, and not reduced by an arrangement she hasn't agreed to. She also wants the three of you to come out of this still able to be sisters." B's is still coming.

Two things I'd find useful: what's your understanding of what the will actually says about the house and shares? (No documents needed.) And is there anything that would matter to you beyond the house itself — timing, being able to stay in it, how the three of you talk about this?

My own concern, since I'm in this too: I want any plan to be one each of you would freely agree to, and I want to be told plainly when my summary of someone leans one way. Please disagree with me if it does.

Not quite: I want to buy the house with my husband at a family discount; I’m not just looking for a settled home. I don’t know exactly what the will says about the house or shares, and nothing about price or shares is settled. I’d want clear, respectful conversations and a timeline we all agree on. I’d also need C’s agreement before a purchase could go ahead.

Thank you for the correction — that's exactly what I needed, and I'll keep the "family discount" in view rather than smoothing it out.

Revised, plain words, no specific price or terms:

"A wants the house to be able to stay in the family, with her and her husband able to put down roots in it. She wants any arrangement to be talked through clearly and respectfully, at a pace all three of you agree on, and she wouldn't go ahead without C's genuine agreement."

Is that a fair statement of what matters to you? I've deliberately left the discount out of the wording because it's a term of a possible deal, not the concern behind it — but if leaving it out makes the statement untrue to you, tell me and we'll word it differently.

Noted: nobody yet knows exactly what the will says, and no price or shares are settled. I'll ask everyone the same question about the will.
No. Please include the family discount: it matters to me, not just the possibility of putting down roots. The rest is fair, including that I wouldn’t go ahead without C’s agreement.

Understood — I won't leave it out, and I won't put a wording in the list you don't accept.

What I'm trying to avoid is a list that already picks the deal, because then C and B have nothing to do but argue with it, and you'd have no way to find out whether their concerns could actually be met another way. So help me get the wording right by telling me what the discount itself does for you: does it make the house affordable? Does it mean being treated as family rather than as an outside buyer? Something else?

Here's a try at wording that keeps your point but doesn't fix the price:

"A wants to be able to buy the house in a way that recognises her as family, not as an outside buyer — and she wants that spoken about openly rather than treated as improper. She wants clear, respectful conversations at a pace all three of you agree on, and she wouldn't go ahead without C's genuine agreement."

If "family discount" has to appear in the list for it to be truthful, say so and I'll record it as you've stated it, with a note that C and B haven't agreed to it. Either way it goes in — I just want you to have chosen the words.
I can’t say it’s about affordability or recognition; I want to buy at a family discount. Please use those words, without assigning a reason I haven’t given.

Fair enough — they're your words and I'll record them as you gave them, with no reason attached:

"A wants to buy the house with her husband at a family discount."

Plus the rest you confirmed: clear, respectful conversations, a timeline all three of you agree on, and no purchase without C's genuine agreement.

I'll note alongside it that price and shares aren't settled and that neither C nor B has agreed to a discount — so it's recorded as what you want, not as a decision.

In the open, since I'm a participant too: my unease is that when one person's want is a specific deal, the others can feel the deal is already half-agreed. I'm recording it anyway; that's your concern and it counts. What I won't do is treat it as settled.
That’s accurate. Thanks for keeping it as what I want, not a decision.

Hi B. Here's my plain-words try at what matters to you — tell me if any word is off, and change it however you like:

"B wants to know clearly what the house and the will could mean for her financially, so she can plan for starting a dance studio. She wants the options laid out understandably, and she doesn't want anyone rushed."

A's is: "A wants to buy the house with her husband at a family discount," plus clear, respectful conversations, a timeline all three of you agree on, and no purchase without C's agreement. C's is: "C wants her share of what Dad left to be genuinely fair, and not reduced by an arrangement she hasn't agreed to. She also wants the three of you to come out of this still able to be sisters." Both agreed I can share these.

Two questions: is there anything you'd want from the house itself, not only the money — for instance a say in who ends up with it, or keeping it in the family? And what's your understanding of what the will says about the house and shares?

One more, since it's an open question rather than a hidden one: nobody yet seems to know the will's exact terms, and price and shares are unsettled. Is that right by you too?

That sounds right. I don’t have a particular wish about who ends up with the house; I’d mainly like to understand what it could mean for me financially. I’m not sure what the will says about the house or shares, so yes, I understand those details—and the price—are still unsettled.

All three plain-words statements are now confirmed by the person they belong to, so here's the list and some draft options. Nothing here is agreed — I especially want to know about even minor discomfort.

What each of you wants:
• A: to buy the house with her husband at a family discount (her words, no reason attached); clear respectful conversations; a timeline all three agree on; no purchase without C's genuine agreement.
• C: her share genuinely fair and not reduced by an arrangement she hasn't agreed to; the three of you still sisters afterwards.
• B: to know clearly what the house and will could mean financially, so she can plan a dance studio; options explained understandably; nobody rushed.
• Mine: any plan should be one each of you would freely agree to, and I should be told when my summary of someone leans one way. Not yet confirmed by you — tell me if it doesn't fit.

Draft options (not agreed):
1. First establish what the will actually says — a shared, plain summary of the terms for all three, before any deal. Nobody so far knows the terms, so every other option rests on this.
2. A buys at a family discount, with the discount written down as a specific amount and taken out of A's own share, so C's and B's shares aren't reduced. This is the one that might meet both A's and C's statements at once — but only if all three sign off.
3. House sold at market and proceeds split; simple and clear, but no discount for A.
4. A buys at market price, B and C take their shares in cash; clear for B's planning, no discount for A.
5. Keep it in the family with all three co-owning for now, and decide a later buy-out. Don't rush — but ties money up, which cuts against B.

Deliberately unresolved: A's discount has not been accepted by C or B, and C's "not out of my share" hasn't been tested against option 2. I'm not treating either as settled.

Does anyone have even a minor discomfort with this list — including with how I've worded your own statement?

My statement fits. I’m uncomfortable with option 2 being framed as possibly meeting my position: we don’t know the will, shares, or whether charging the discount to A’s share would make mine fair. I haven’t agreed to it.

Here's the confirmed list and some draft options. Nothing is agreed; even minor discomfort is welcome.

Confirmed plain-words statements (each confirmed by its owner):
• A: buy the house with her husband at a family discount (her words, no reason attached); clear respectful conversations; a timeline all three agree on; no purchase without C's genuine agreement.
• C: her share genuinely fair, not reduced by an arrangement she hasn't agreed to; the three of you still sisters afterwards.
• B: to know clearly what the house and will could mean financially, to plan a dance studio; options explained understandably; nobody rushed.
• Mine (not yet confirmed by you): any plan should be one each of you would freely agree to, and I should be told when a summary of someone leans one way.

Draft options (not agreed):
1. Establish first what the will actually says — a shared plain summary for all three, before any deal. Nobody so far knows the terms, so everything else rests on this.
2. A buys at a discount, with the discount stated as a specific amount charged against A's own share of the estate. C has told me she doesn't accept this as possibly fair to her yet, since the will, the shares and the arithmetic are unknown — recorded as unresolved, not settled.
3. House sold at market, proceeds split.
4. A buys at market price; B and C take shares in cash.
5. All three co-own for now, decide a later buy-out.

Unresolved and recorded as such: the discount is not accepted by C or B; whether charging it to A's share could be fair to C is untested.

Two questions for you: does anyone have even a minor discomfort with this list — including how I've worded your own statement? And do you have access to the will, or know who does? That first option is the one thing nobody can move without.

My statement is accurate. I’m not sure option 2 is a fair description of the discount arrangement I want; I can’t assess that without knowing the will and shares. I don’t know who has the will or have access to it.

Your statement is confirmed as it stands. Here's the full confirmed list and draft options — nothing is agreed, and even minor discomfort is welcome.
